data.long_meaning: The name Rakib is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Rakta' which means 'blood'. This name is believed to be a symbol of power, strength and courage. It is a name given to a ruler or a warrior, who holds the power to protect and rule. The name Rakib carries the meaning “Holder of power” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Bengali, Hindi. Parents who choose Rakib usually hope their child will grow to embody holder of power and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Rakib belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Holder of power.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rakib total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

historical_references.reference: According to Hindu mythology, Rakib is a variant of the name Raktabija, which means 'one who causes the dropping of blood'. Raktabija was a demon who could create as many corpses as drops of his blood fell, making him virtually invincible. He was slain by Lord Krishna during the Mahabharata war, using a weapon that absorbed every drop of his blood.

Another reference to Rakib is found in Jain literature, where he is mentioned as a Yaksha (nature spirit) who enjoyed dancing during the Rajgira Mahotsava (Rajgira festival) held for Mahavira. This event is believed to have taken place around 500 BCE.
